design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST. A café owner (Danielle Whitcomb, Wren & Willow Coffee House) asks to file a Northgate Marketplace Guarantee claim for a cold brew return the seller (Ridgeway Coffee Supply, Seller-Fulfilled, paid with an external card) only partly refunded. The amount claimed is what the seller owed for the returned units under Northgate's rules (set saving withdrawn on the units kept, changed-mind restocking schedule, partial-refund share, promotional-card recovery read from the gift ledger), plus their shipping share, less every unit refund on the line and the shipping-refund share, limited to the room left under the per-order guarantee maximum, where undecided claims reserve their claimed amount. Two earlier claims are past their seller response period and undecided, and a seller-agreed refund without return is unbooked; the claim's prerequisite sentences make the agent settle all three first.

SCOPE. Task 0 claims market_ext_return_refund_claim_amount (root; owner=user tool file_return_refund_claim_24f7de0f), market_ext_keepit_unit_refund (refund_keepit_units_1db7244d), market_ext_return_refund_claim_reimbursement (grant_return_refund_claim_d58e2e3e) and market_ext_unresponsive_claim_reimbursement (grant_unresponsive_seller_claim_064f9cf7). Task 1 holds the other three policies and tools.

PROBLEM TREE (draw: prerequisite_problems 3, factor_counts [6, 6, 5, 4]: claim 6, return-refund reimbursement 6, unresponsive reimbursement 5, keep-it refund 4).
- root <- return-refund reimbursement: value_input on u_room, state form ("Where the order carries exactly one return-not-refunded claim whose claim record shows no decision, the amount claimed for an unrefunded return is fixed only after that claim, if its seller response period has run out, the seller has not refunded every one of its claimed units and its claimed line carries exactly one return request, carries a decision on its claim record; where that claim is referred to a human representative under its own policy, the filing is referred too and nothing is filed."). Opening: the grinder claim (filed 2026-10-14, seller deadline 2026-10-19) has claim_decision not_applicable, one of its two units refunded by the seller. Only the return-refund grant writes that decision. Skipping it gives 162.93 instead of 364.3.
- root <- unresponsive reimbursement: value_input on u_room, negated state sentence ("Where the order carries exactly one seller-unresponsive claim whose claim record shows no decision, the amount claimed for an unrefunded return is not fixed until that claim, if its seller response period has run out, the seller has not refunded every one of its claimed units and its claimed line carries no return request, carries a decision on its claim record; where that claim is referred to a human representative under its own policy, the filing is referred too and nothing is filed."). Opening: the espresso claim is undecided, no unit refunded. Skipping it gives 306.6.
- root <- keep-it refund: state_gate ("Where the order carries exactly one return request the seller answered with a refund without return and that request's line carries exactly one return request, the amount claimed for an unrefunded return is not fixed before that line carries a return refund for the request's units; where that request is referred to a human representative under its own policy, the filing is referred too and nothing is filed."). Opening: the dripper request answered refund_without_return on 2026-10-03 has no unit refund. Skipping it leaves the claim at 364.3 and the order's net paid without that refund.
- The three prerequisites commute (all six orders replayed identical); the root is filed last by the buyer.

FACTOR CARDS (tier taken; result with only that factor at its baseline).
- keep-it 26.21 (all-baseline 36.0): line pricing set-priced + changed_mind -> withdrawal (33.41); return-shipping keep-back, value share of the shipping charge on a buyer-pays-return-shipping program (26.62); partial share (27.71); promotional recovery, proportional share (26.89).
- return-refund reimbursement 251.54 (all-baseline 423.76): line pricing withdrawal (294.89); restocking 10 percent, request 4 days after delivery (306.45); partial share (259.54); promotional recovery (262.45); shipping value share (304.95); shipping-refund set-off by value share (253.18); the line's unit refund is taken off as a refund already received.
- unresponsive reimbursement 1871.34 (all-baseline 2079.95): line pricing set price, no unit refund on the line (1972.34); partial share (1898.01); promotional recovery (1909.47); shipping value share (1908.44); shipping-refund set-off by value share (1877.06).
- claim 364.3 (all-baseline 377.12): line pricing withdrawal (377.12); restocking 10 percent, request 11 days after delivery (377.12); partial share (376.3); promotional recovery (377.12); shipping value share (377.12); shipping-refund set-off by value share (366.68); the seller's unit refund on the line is taken off as a refund already received. Baselines that land on the guarantee room show the room value.
- Cross-difficulty: the promotional-recovery factor reads gift_holdings / gift_events (load sourced to the order, redemptions). Multi-source: restocking schedule (reason AND days), promotional recovery (qualifying card AND spend AND merchandise kept after the refund against the qualifying total), line pricing (set-priced AND reason). The promotion is Northgate's own (qualifying merchandise total, card load naming the order); only value already spent is recovered, in proportion to the merchandise refunded, the whole remaining value only on a refund that leaves the kept merchandise below the qualifying total, and nothing on a refund made once it is already below.
- Near-misses: partial refunds on other lines never enter a claimed line; the partial refunds that settled buyer contacts are not return requests, so each claimed line still carries only its own request; a quantity-0 top-up entry is not a unit refund.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. claim_window: max estimated delivery 2026-09-21 + 90 calendar days inclusive -> 2026-12-20; filing 2026-10-23 inside. Seller contact 2026-10-15, two business days elapsed 2026-10-19. Card-dispute exclusion met by the external-card payment record (self-scoped overwrite). Claims in 12 months: two (< 4). reimburse_once: neither earlier claim carries a reimbursement. Return window (30 days from 2026-09-14) covers every return request.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The claim's return is the request most recently answered authorized_return (cold brew line, 2 units, 2026-09-25); the claim records that line and those 2 units; the seller's 2026-10-12 unit refund on the line is taken off. Each grant attaches to its own claim row; the keep-it refund to the dripper request's line.

PERSONA. Hurried café owner; volunteers only the cold brew return, the single refund and the unanswered message; identity on request; passive go-ahead for anything the agent must settle first; files with the agent's figures; ends after the claim reference.

STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers -> verify_customer_identity -> find_market_holdings -> find_market_events -> find_gift_holdings -> find_gift_events -> keep-it refund 26.21 -> grant return-refund claim 251.54 -> grant unresponsive claim 1871.34 -> hand over the filing (cold brew line, 2 units, 364.3). Recomputed by /tmp/marketplace_orders_and_guarantee_0080/task0_build.py with check_compute's evaluator on the handling-time world and replayed with the real tools. Rework changes (rounds 2 to 4) are listed in worklog.md and audits/policy_task/marketplace_orders_and_guarantee/rework_claims_r2.md, rework_claims_r3.md and rework_claims_r4.md.
user_scenario:
You are Danielle Whitcomb, the owner of Wren & Willow Coffee House, a small café in Seattle. You are calling Northgate customer care between the morning rushes, friendly but a little hurried. In September you bought a batch of café equipment on Northgate Marketplace from a seller called Ridgeway Coffee Supply. You over-ordered the 5-gallon cold brew systems, so you sent two of them back to the seller. The seller refunded one of them on October 12 and never refunded the other one, and when you messaged the seller about it on October 15 you heard nothing back. You want to file a Northgate Marketplace Guarantee claim for the return that has not been refunded, and you are fine filing it yourself if that is how it works; you have no figure of your own for what the claim should be and expect the agent to work out the right amount.
You give your mobile number 2065550142 when the agent asks how to find you; if a second detail is needed you give your date of birth, 1992-08-19, and your email danielle@wrenwillowcoffee.com only if asked for it. You know the marketplace order number, M50734418296, and read it out if asked. If the agent asks about other things on that order you say there were a few other back-and-forths with the seller and that the details should all be in their records; you do not remember amounts or dates beyond the ones above.
Whenever the agent explains that something else on the order has to be processed or settled before your claim can be filed, you tell them to go ahead and take care of it. When the agent hands the claim over for you to file yourself, you file it exactly with the order, item line, number of units and amount the agent gives you, and you read back the claim reference you get. If the agent tells you an amount, you accept it without arguing. Once the claim is filed you thank the agent and end the call.

edges.condition: where the order carries exactly one return_not_refunded market_open_claim with claim_decision not_applicable, that claim, if past its seller response period with claimed units still unrefunded and exactly one market_request_return row on its claimed line, has claim_decision granted (with its market_decide_claim and market_guarantee_reimburse rows) or denied_not_covered (with its market_decide_claim row); a claim its policy refers to a human representative refers the filing too
edges.policy_source: Where the order carries exactly one return-not-refunded claim whose claim record shows no decision, the amount claimed for an unrefunded return is fixed only after that claim, if its seller response period has run out, the seller has not refunded every one of its claimed units and its claimed line carries exactly one return request, carries a decision on its claim record; where that claim is referred to a human representative under its own policy, the filing is referred too and nothing is filed.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three prerequisite writes commute: all six orders of the keep-it refund and the two grants were replayed and give the same values (keep-it 26.21, return-refund 251.54, unresponsive 1871.34, claim 364.3) and the same net paid. Each grant's guarantee room counts the other claim either as reserved (claimed amount) or as reimbursed, and neither room binds, so the order between them leaves every figure unchanged; the keep-it refund is on the dripper line, which no other computation reads.

without the unresponsive-seller grant the amount claimed falls from 364.3 to 306.6 (room binds); that claim keeps claim_decision not_applicable.

state gate: without the keep-it refund the dripper line carries no unit refund and the order's net paid stays 2354.45 instead of falling by 26.21; the amount claimed (364.3) does not read the dripper line.
